text:
Marie: Quick question — sizing for a Dedicated pool running a 30B family model. We want steady-state ~5k rps inference (short responses), target p95 latency <= 120ms for eu-west and us-west. Any rough GPU counts if we assume q4 quant and kernel mix (triton/flash_attn)?

Chris: Are requests uniform or bursty? important for concurrency targets. also which sequence len?

Marie: Mostly short, median tokens ~32, 95th tokens ~128. Traffic is mildly bursty (2x peak for 30s). Need steady throughput + room for spikes.

Devon: Did an offline sim this morning. With q4_0, sequence=128, and batcher tuned to 16 sequences / GPU: A100-40GB -> ~220 rps per GPU p95 ~110ms (flash_attn). V100-ish slower.

Devon: TL;DR numbers from sim:
```
model: 30B-q4
seq: 128
batch_per_gpu: 16
A100-40: rps=220 p95=110ms
H100-80: rps=360 p95=95ms
T4: rps=95 p95=230ms
```

Sara: Region delta: eu-west tests had slightly worse cold-kv hit rates due to cross-az routing; add ~10% headroom in eu-west. Also kernel builds differ — h100 kernels give better perf at 8-bit.

Ben: For Dedicated we usually add 20% autoscale headroom and configure burst capacity (reserve extra 10% warm GPUs). So baseline GPUs = ceil(required / rps_per_gpu) * 1.2 then round up for burst.

Marie: So rough calc? using H100 numbers from Devon for 5k rps: 5000/360 ~= 14 GPUs -> with 20% headroom = 17, plus burst config -> 19?

Devon: Yup that math checks. If you prefer A100 baseline: 5000/220 ~= 23 -> with 20% = 28 -> burst -> 31.

Chris: Ops question — what's the desired concurrency per GPU? If we push concurrency too high we lose p95. I recommend target_concurrency = 8-12 for H100; tuning can go to 16 but watch tail latency.

Marie: Noted. What about quantization risk — do we expect quality regressions running q4_0 vs q8? need to sign off with evaluations before commit.

Devon: We ran eval set of 2k prompts: q4_0 regression within noise for chat/clf but edge-case math answer accuracy dipped ~2%. Recommend running production evals and enabling fallback to fp16 on the small fraction of requests flagged by evals.

Sara: Ops-config snippet for autoscale we used (copy):
```
autoscale:
  min: 8
  baseline: 17
  max: 40
  scale_step: 2
  cooldown_s: 120
  burst_reserve: 3
```

Ben: Cost note: H100 per-hour calc depends on commit pricing but rough on-demand math: 19 H100 ~ costly. Consider mixed pool: primary H100s + cheaper A100 or T4s for background/low-priority workloads. Use routing policy to prefer H100 for high-SLO routes.

Marie: Good call. Can someone run a short canary (eu-west) with ~10 gpus H100 and monitor p99/p95 and KV hit ratio? I'll open a ticket for model-eval gating. @Devon can you kick it off?

Devon: On it. I'll spin 10 H100s in eu-west, run load script for 2k rps for 10m and post results.

ops-bot: deploy: canary pool started (pool-id: dedicated-canary-30b-eu). 10 H100 allocated.

Marie: Thanks — please paste the latency/time series and the sample failure cases here after the run. :thumbsup:

Ben: FYI I'll draft a cost vs SLO doc comparing 17 H100 vs 28 A100 and include regional price deltas.

Chris: If the canary looks good, plan a staged ramp: 10 -> 17 -> 25 over 48h with traffic-weighted rollout and automatic fallback to smaller model if p95 > 150ms.

Marie: Sounds like a plan. We'll reconvene after canary data.

Devon: starting load in 2m. I will annotate the run with the kernel variants (flash_attn vs triton) to see tail differences.

ops-bot: load-test: job-558 running (target=2000 rps, duration=10m). Logs will be uploaded to: https://internal.redwood/logs/job-558

Marie: Thanks all. Keeping notes here for capacity planning doc.
